gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Duex Max DS, its top pick for a laptop with one USB-C port, has no power pass-through. It fills the laptop's only USB-C port and draws its power from the laptop, so a laptop that charges over USB-C can't charge while the screen is connected. The Trio 3 Pro takes the laptop's charger in a second USB-C port and passes power on to the laptop (65 W per its listing). Running both of its screens from one cable needs Mobile Pixels' display driver.
standout_why: Pages compared: the two cited pages, mobilepixels.us/products/trio and itechguides.com/best-laptop-screen-extenders-in-2025. I could not open the Trio page; the store and its tools returned HTTP 429. I also compared our own dealectric.com/best-laptop-screen-extender and the uncited deskgearhq.com guide. itechguides gives 65 W pass-through for the Trio 3 Pro and says nothing on pass-through for any Duex. Our own page gives the Duex Max DS a 4.5 W draw but says nothing on pass-through. The deskgearhq guide puts a '–' in its pass-through column for the Duex Max and never explains the dash. Its review page, which says 'No power pass-through' outright, was not among ChatGPT's results. No page links the missing pass-through to the one-port case: the screen and the charger need the same port.
decides: Some laptops charge only through their one USB-C port. On those, the Duex Max DS (ChatGPT's first-chat top pick) can't run without draining the battery, unless the laptop also has HDMI and a USB-A port. In that case HDMI carries the video and the USB-C cable plugs into the laptop's USB-A port through the included adapter, which leaves the USB-C port free for the charger. The Trio 3 Pro keeps the laptop charging through the screen's second USB-C port. On one port it needs Mobile Pixels' driver to run both screens. Pick by the laptop's other ports: HDMI plus USB-A makes the Duex Max DS work; USB-C only points to the Trio 3 Pro.
